requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from structural
hashes. Decorators participate in the decorated declaration's hash along
with its other source structure and text.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.fingerprints` has no implementation edges and no review roots. Every clause states observable behavior, so none needs implementation evidence.

- "Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words": this fixes the digest value. Any library or code path that produces the same SHA-256 digest satisfies it. A different digest would change the output, which is a behavioral difference. The encoding rules themselves belong to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which only cites here. They are not a structural obligation of this requirement.
- "The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version": this is the scheme string the TypeScript provider reports. The trait signature `fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str` is prescribed by the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, not by this text. Any code that returns the same identifier behaves identically.
- "Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from structural hashes": this describes which inputs affect the hash. An implementation that drops comments by any mechanism gives the same hashes.
- "Decorators participate in the decorated declaration's hash along with its other source structure and text": this also describes hash inputs. It does not prescribe a type, field, signature or delegation. Including them through a sibling-attachment rule or through the declaration's own subtree gives the same hash.

No clause prescribes a library, algorithm structure, type, signature or delegation that an alternative could violate while keeping the same observable results. Tests can check the hash behavior.

behavioral: The tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.fingerprints`. Implementation source was not needed.

**Comments are excluded, including documentation comments.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` covers `a.ts` and `a.tsx`.
- The base source has a `/** docs */` comment. The edited source has `/** other docs */` and the same code with extra whitespace in a string. The test asserts equal fingerprints.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` covers `a.ts` with line comments (`// note`) and block comments (`/* inline */`). Changing the comment text, or removing the comments, leaves the hash unchanged. Changing a non-comment token (`1` to `2`) changes it.

**Whitespace-separated words, so `two words` differs from `twowords`.** The same bundled test asserts `assert_ne!` between the original and a `twowords` variant for `.ts` and `.tsx`. It also checks that the fingerprint is 64 hex characters, which is consistent with SHA-256. The SHA-256 algorithm and the encoding rules come from the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, so I did not reassess them here.

**Fingerprint scheme identifies the rules and version.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` and its helper `fn[check]` assert `typescript-structural-v2` for `languages::TypeScript` and `tsx-structural-v2` for `languages::Tsx`. They also assert that content loaded through the inferred and the explicit language carries the same scheme.

**Decorators participate in the decorated declaration's hash.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[typescript_and_tsx_decorators_belong_to_the_decorated_declaration]` runs for both `.ts` and `.tsx`. It covers class decorators, method decorators (including a multi-line call decorator), an `export default abstract class` with a decorator, and a nested decorated class.
- Renaming a decorator, changing a decorator argument, replacing a decorator with different content, and removing a decorator all change `structural_hash()` and `fingerprint()` of the declaration.
- Changing `@trace` to `@logged` changes the method's fingerprint and the enclosing class's `structural_hash`, but not the class's identity `fingerprint`, which is the intended split.

I found no obligation without a test that asserts its outcome.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from structural
hashes. Decorators participate in the decorated declaration's hash along
with its other source structure and text.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
